findings.title: All app modules are still eagerly imported at module evaluation time
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the values in `appStore` are `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, etc., rather than functions like `() => import("./applecalendar")`. Because `import(...)` is called directly when constructing the `appStore` object literal, every single app package is still loaded and evaluated immediately as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, defeating the purpose of lazy/on-demand async imports. Additionally, if any of those dynamic imports reject at startup before being awaited, it will trigger an unhandled promise rejection. Each entry should be a thunk (`() => import(...)`) invoked only when that specific app is requested.

findings.title: `forEach` with `async` callback populates `apiDeletes` after `Promise.all` is already reached
findings.body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an `async` callback inside `.forEach()`. Because `.forEach()` does not await promises returned by its callback, execution immediately continues past the `if (bookingCalendarReference)` block right after the first `await getCalendar(credential)` suspends. As a result, `apiDeletes` is still empty (or incomplete) when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) or `await apiDeletes` (line 617) runs, so the calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are not awaited and may be terminated early in serverless environments or fail silently without being caught.

findings.title: Async `forEach` inside `try/catch` will not await calendar/video deletions or catch errors
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try/catch` block. Because `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await the promises returned by an `async` callback, `Reschedule` will proceed to send emails and return `true` before `getCalendar` and `calendar.deleteEvent` complete, and any rejection inside the async callback will become an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead. (The same issue is present in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` at line 125 and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` at line 553.)
